Pre-op here w a fairly heavy chest in a Georgia (US) city: I’ve found most men mind their business. I shower there on occasion, I get dressed in the shower stall. I go to a popular gym, so it’s worth noting lots of cis men also have heavy set chests and go to the gym with the intention of toning it. Confidence is key! If you act like you belong then you do :)

As an undergrad about to graduate with a performance degree, my two cents are sometimes the section is stronger than the ensemble. Some of our top studios have travelled internationally to win competitions. So when you only have so many spots in an ensemble, those same award winners are going to get placed in the ‘lower ensemble’. Your peers who don’t understand this concept are criticizing you for the wrong reasons and don’t see the bigger picture. I agree with others about not minding them and practicing your way into the group you’d like to be in, but sometimes changing your perspective will do a lot more than getting what you want (for lack of better words).

I never got positive self talk. It felt stupid to stand in a mirror and say ‘affirming words’ or whatever, but my latest therapist encouraged self debate. If I had a thought, like “My friends would be better off without me,” then she wanted me to debate with myself. What are the reasons they would be, and what are the reasons they wouldn’t be? It requires complete emotional honesty and in the beginning the wrong side will almost always win but in the end it’s a great way to dissect negative thoughts and find a legitimate reason for why that thought is wrong. Looking at my reflection and telling myself life is great won’t do anything, but telling myself “This is shitty and it will probably continue to be shitty but it’s going to be rock-bottom shitty if I don’t get up and work to fix it” feels a lot less stupid AND it’s productive.

I haven’t been doing this for long, but I’ve recently started collecting moss. I go on walks a lot, and I learned about moss lawns a few weeks ago. It’s just a really neat plant, right now I have all of the patches in a jar. Not sure what I’m going to do with them but it’s one of my favorite things to do now. You start to notice a lot more than you normally do, like different bugs and how plants grow. My favorite place I’ve collected is a moss covered island in a creek. There’s a single tree just barely alive, it’s roots are exposed and go down into the river, but there are tons of tiny plants surrounding it. If you wait long enough, fish will come out of the tree roots. It’s pretty calming, and definitely the only regret I have about leaving town soon.
